# FAIR-bioHeaders Tools (Java)

> Java library for reading, checksum-verifying and JSON-Schema-validating FAIR-bioHeaders provenance headers embedded in bioinformatics files: FHR for reference genome FASTA and GFA, FHP for protein FASTA, and FHGFF3 for GFF3 annotations. A header is a block of YAML lines at the top of the file (`;~` in FASTA, `#~` in GFA and GFF3), validated against a draft/2020-12 JSON Schema and covered by a SHA-512/256 checksum of the file's exact bytes. This repository is the Java member of the per-language library family; the normative definitions are in FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification and the reference implementation with header writing is the Python `fair-bioheaders` toolkit.

Key facts (this library bundles contract copies of FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification v0.6.0 as its current release; selection follows the shared rules V1-V6):

- Schema versions: FHR `schemaVersion: '2.1'`, FHP `'1.2'`, FHGFF3 `'1.2'`; cite the versioned w3id URLs `https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/{fhr,fhp,fhgff3}/v0.6.0`. A file's `schema` value selects the schema it is validated against; an unknown release is reported as unsupported-version, never re-checked against another schema.
- **Never write or edit a checksum by hand.** This library only verifies (read + validate + checksum-verify); header creation belongs to `bioheaders combine` in the Python toolkit. Changing any byte except the checksum line invalidates it.
- The checksum is SHA-512/256 (the JDK `MessageDigest` algorithm, not truncated SHA-512) over the file's exact bytes minus the one root-level `checksum` line and its terminator, padded standard base64, compared as exact strings (FORMAT.md R1-R5). Gzip/bgzip files are verified through their decompressed bytes.
- In FASTA, header values containing `>` or `@` should be written as YAML escapes `\x3E` and `\x40` (rule R11), because kseq-based readers start a record at those characters; a file with raw characters stays valid and this reader warns. YAML readers return the real characters.
- Many FASTA tools reject a leading `;~` block, including samtools faidx (htslib), pysam `FastaFile`, bedtools getfasta, Picard, Bowtie2, HISAT2, STAR, salmon and Biopython's default `fasta` format. Use `bioheaders strip` (Python toolkit) to make a plain copy, or `SeqIO.parse(path, "fasta-pearson")` in Biopython. GFF3 and GFA tools surveyed accept `#~` lines.
- Plain YAML scalars must read identically under YAML 1.1 and YAML 1.2 (rule R12): `010`, `1_000`, `1:30`, `yes`, `1e3` and explicit tags are invalid; the reader enforces this with its own resolver pinned to the reference toolkit's behavior, not the parser's.
- Extension fields (rule R15, from FHR 2.1 and FHP/FHGFF3 1.1): top-level `^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` keys are accepted and carry no standard meaning; every other unknown key is invalid and nested objects stay closed.
- No schema is released for FHT or FHGM (drafts, rule V7): no `schemaVersion`, no w3id URL, no registry row. Header types are registry data (`schemas/bundled.json` `types`). **FHT is registered as a pinned draft** (FHT-Specification commit 226f923c28b680edb3c546e99a751482d06aef1a, SHA-256 59ad9641adcb0e5591045c2d894c066d1adc9984cca84c5ff6502f8dad88487e): readable only through explicit opt-in (`Options.builder().enableDraftContracts(true)`, `verify --experimental-drafts`, `--draft FHT`, system property `org.fairbioheaders.experimental.drafts`, environment variable `FAIR_BIOHEADERS_EXPERIMENTAL_DRAFTS`), re-digest-checked at bundle build, and warned on per record with the commit and digest named. Gate closed = rule V5 (read as FHR, near-miss warning), byte-identical to the released-only reader. Reading a draft is not adoption, support or release, and its 72 vectors are counted in a separate labelled job, never in the 291. **FHGM is registered as an `embedded-records` draft**: it is not a header type - its records ride inside an FHGFF3 header under `x-fhgm-models`, the file stays routed by its released FHGFF3 citation, and `FhgmModels` (opt-in, two further pinned contract files, each with its own commit: record contract `bf1553ca…` at commit `ac3d37b3…`, transport overlay `d1619cce…` (2 613 B, the dual-base overlay) at commit `5d15ccc1…`, both of FHGM-Specification) applies the draft's model-level rules K1-K6, refusing any carrier whose base schema or checksum fails first (B1). Its 43 vectors and 10 rule tests run in the labelled draft job; the suite's separate FHGFF3-1.2 `base_matrix.json` lane is not run here. See docs/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md.

## Using it

```java
import org.fairbioheaders.BioHeaders;
import org.fairbioheaders.VerifyResult;

VerifyResult r = new BioHeaders().verifyFile(Path.of("genome.fhr.fasta"));
r.isValid(); r.status();          // VALID | INVALID | UNSUPPORTED_VERSION
r.computedChecksum();             // recomputed SHA-512/256 (R3/R4)
r.metadata();                     // parsed header as a Jackson JsonNode
r.issues();                       // rule-labelled errors and warnings (R11, R14, V5, V6, V7)
r.parentLinkVerdicts();           // CHECKED_PASS | CHECKED_FAIL | UNCHECKED, per derivedFrom entry
```

CLI: `java -cp target/classes:<deps> org.fairbioheaders.cli.Main verify FILE...` (exit 0 only when every file verifies).

## Scope boundaries

- Implemented: containers FASTA/GFA/GFF3, FORMAT.md R1-R8 and R10-R14, FHGFF3.md G1-G3 placement and contract checks, SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V1-V6 selection plus the opt-in V7 draft lane (FHT and FHGM, pinned), draft/2020-12 validation with format assertions, per-entry `derivedFrom` parent-link verdicts (`ParentLinks`, `verify --parent`), bundled frozen schema copies v0.3.0-v0.6.0 and three pinned draft contract files, all with SHA-256 provenance.
- Not implemented: header writing, conversion, stripping, faidx, HTML microdata and JSON-LD bindings, and GFF3 feature-line validation (use gff3-validator). FHGM records are read only through the pinned opt-in draft lane - never as support. `docs/STATUS.md` records the shared-conformance results (228 embedded-header vectors run; the 63 microdata/JSON-LD vectors are declared not run) and the separate draft-lane results (72 FHT vectors, 43 FHGM vectors, plus FHGM's 1.2 matrix lane declared not run); `docs/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md` is the type × operation × serialization × version statement with every hole named.
- Acceptance is the shared 291-vector conformance suite of FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification (`conformance/manifest.json`); run with `./mvnw test -Dfh.spec.dir=<spec-checkout>`. Default behavior is additionally pinned by a committed fingerprint of the released-contract reading (`src/test/resources/golden/default-behavior-v0.6.0.json`, `DefaultBehaviorGoldenTest`).
